title: Shiroishi — 白石
goal: Distinguish distance, height and price, and recognise adjective tense.

cards.title: Reusing Both Characters of a City Name

blocks.text: Shiroishi is associated with Shiroishi Castle and its castle-town setting. Our shop and map exercises are invented; they do not give real walking distances or admission prices.
**白石に行きました。** しろいしに いきました。 — I went to Shiroishi.

We can recognise both name characters from earlier lessons. That is the reward of cumulative learning: we spend less effort decoding a familiar shape and more effort expressing a new relationship. The whole place reading still matters even when its components are already known.

items: **Character:** 白 · **Meaning/readings:** white; しろ; 白い = しろい; ハク · **Radical/components:** 白, しろ; short upper stroke over the enclosed lower section · **Role:** Review from Matsushima.
**Character:** 石 · **Meaning/readings:** stone; いし; セキ/シャク · **Radical/components:** 石, いし; upper strokes and a lower 口-like section · **Role:** Review from Morioka.

blocks.text: **白石 / しろいし** is a name. **白い石 / しろいいし** is the ordinary phrase “a white stone.” The adjective's extra い matters. Do not omit it in the ordinary description merely because the place name uses 白 directly before 石. Character glosses alone do not establish the name's origin.

**近い / ちかい — near; 駅に近い / えきにちかい — near the station.** Radical **辶**, しんにょう, with **斤** inside. 辶 provides a movement/route-related connection; 斤 is associated with historical sound structure. Notice the same 斤 shape that helped identify 新.
**この店は駅に近いです。** この みせは えきに ちかいです。 — This shop is near the station.
Here 駅に gives the reference point for “near.” It is neither the action-place で nor a time. Ask “near what?” before choosing a particle. 近い is an い-adjective, not an existence verb.

**遠い / とおい — far; 駅から遠い / えきからとおい — far from the station.** Radical **辶**, しんにょう, with **袁** inside, a historical sound element. Its inner strokes are recognition pieces; we do not require the learner to use 袁 as a standalone word.
**あの店は駅から遠いです。** あの みせは えきから とおいです。 — That shop over there is far from the station.

Contrast the fictional map: this shop is near the station; the other is far from it. から marks the reference point “from” here, extending its familiar origin use. Being far does not tell us whether the shop is expensive.
**高い / たかい — high; expensive.** 高 is its own radical, たかい. Its stacked modern shape is building-derived; the several enclosed sections are not three independent 口 words added together.
**あの山は高いです。** あの やまは たかいです。 — That mountain is high.
**この本は高いです。** この ほんは たかいです。 — This book is expensive.

The noun and context select the ordinary English meaning. A mountain has height; a shop book has a price. Do not infer “expensive mountain” in our landscape sentence. We practise both common uses without adding obscure compounds.

**安い / やすい — cheap; inexpensive.** Radical **宀**, うかんむり, above **女**. These visible components help recognise 安. A remembered picture of a roof and person is a mnemonic, not a rule about people's social roles or the price of houses.
**この本は安いです。** この ほんは やすいです。 — This book is inexpensive.

**安い本 / やすいほん — an inexpensive book.** 安 has other meanings in compounds, but our word here concerns price. “Cheap” in this lesson does not automatically mean poor quality. The language expresses the price description; further judgments need context.
Fictional labels: one book costs **三百円 / さんびゃくえん — 300 yen**; another **千二百円 / せんにひゃくえん — 1,200 yen**.
**この本は三百円です。安いです。** この ほんは さんびゃくえんです。やすいです。 — This book is 300 yen. It is inexpensive.
**その本は千二百円です。** その ほんは せんにひゃくえんです。 — That book is 1,200 yen.

Prices are exact quantities in the exercise; 高い/安い are the speaker's judgments. Keep the earlier sound change 三百 = さんびゃく. We do not claim that these are actual shop prices or a universal cheap/expensive threshold.
Unlike a verb, an ordinary い-adjective carries its own changes before polite です:

items: **Meaning:** is inexpensive · **Taught form:** 安いです · **Reading:** やすいです
**Meaning:** is not inexpensive · **Taught form:** 安くないです · **Reading:** やすくないです
**Meaning:** was inexpensive · **Taught form:** 安かったです · **Reading:** やすかったです
**Meaning:** was not inexpensive · **Taught form:** 安くなかったです · **Reading:** やすくなかったです

blocks.text: Remove final い, then add くない, かった, or くなかった as appropriate. Do not construct **安いでした**. This formalises the past-description pattern rather than introducing a new plain-style conversation. The same taught pattern applies to 高い, 近い, 遠い, 新しい and 古い.
**安い本を買いました。** やすい ほんを かいました。 — I bought an inexpensive book.
**この本は安かったです。** この ほんは やすかったです。 — This book was inexpensive.

The first places the completed buying action in the past; the adjective inside the noun phrase is unchanged. The second places the price description in the past. **この店は駅に近くなかったです。** この みせは えきに ちかくなかったです。 — This shop was not near the station.
Read the actual ending rather than assume every past account uses ました. We have not yet introduced all tense patterns for な-adjectives and nouns.

cards.title: A Small Decision in a Shop

blocks.text: **この本はいくらですか。** この ほんは いくらですか。 — How much is this book?
**三百円です。** さんびゃくえんです。 — It is 300 yen.
**この本を買います。** この ほんを かいます。 — I will buy this book.
Then the narrator reports: **白石で安い本を買いました。** しろいしで やすい ほんを かいました。 — I bought an inexpensive book in Shiroishi.
The purchase follows an explicit choice; the story does not introduce a new causal grammar pattern. この still needs the noun 本. A polite question and a simple statement are enough for this scene.

items: Translate 白い石 and read 白石. **Answer:** a white stone, しろいいし; Shiroishi, しろいし.
Read 三百円. **Answer:** さんびゃくえん.
高い with 山 describes what? **Answer:** height.
Make 安いです past. **Answer:** 安かったです.
Make 近いです past negative. **Answer:** 近くなかったです.
Does “not cheap” always mean “expensive”? **Answer:** No; negating one description is not a complete price classification.

blocks.text: 近い is ちかい; 遠い is とおい. Use a supplied reference point for distance. 高い can concern height or price; 安い concerns price in our examples. 安いです/安くないです/安かったです/安くなかったです are four taught descriptions. Do not use 安いでした.
**Recall task:** “I bought an inexpensive book in Shiroishi.” **Model:** 白石で安い本を買いました。 Miyagi's four location lessons are complete. Read its cumulative story and take its test before Akita.
